subject: Pathology
stem: A 58-year-old man with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to aspiration pneumonia is receiving invasive mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit. Initially, he is ventilated using volume-control ventilation with a traditional high tidal volume of 12 mL/kg predicted body weight (850 mL) and zero positive end-expiratory pressure (ZEEP). After 48 hours, his oxygenation deteriorates significantly, and his static compliance drops from 35 mL/cm H2O to 18 mL/cm H2O. Repeat chest CT reveals marked worsening of bilateral alveolar opacities with new interstitial emphysema and subpleural pneumatoceles. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrates a marked increase in protein concentration, neutrophil counts, and high concentrations of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-8). Plasma concentrations of these same cytokines are also markedly elevated, accompanied by new-onset oliguria and hypotension. Which of the following mechanical and biological mechanisms primarily explains how high-tidal-volume mechanical ventilation induced this widespread tissue damage?

options.text: Selective barometric rupture of conducting airway cartilaginous rings without disruption of the peripheral alveolar-capillary gas exchange surface
options.explanation: VILI primarily damages the peripheral alveolar-capillary barrier (diffuse alveolar damage), not large conducting cartilaginous airways.

options.text: Immediate pulmonary arterial thrombosis caused by mechanical compression of extra-alveolar blood vessels by elevated pleural pressure
options.explanation: Mechanical compression of intra-alveolar capillaries increases PVR, but the primary pathology of VILI is epithelial rupture and cytokine release, not macroscopic arterial thrombosis.

options.text: Profound hypocarbic vasoconstriction of systemic coronary arteries secondary to high minute ventilation washing out all carbon dioxide
options.explanation: While hyperventilation can cause hypocapnia, VILI is driven by mechanical alveolar strain and shear stress leading to biotrauma and multiorgan failure.

options.text: Pure allergic anaphylactoid response to silicone polymers shedding from the synthetic inner lumen of the endotracheal tube
options.explanation: Endotracheal tube materials are biocompatible; VILI is a mechanical and mechanotransduction-mediated biological injury.

options.text: Excessive alveolar overdistension at end-inspiration (volutrauma) combined with repetitive cyclic recruitment and derecruitment of unstable alveoli at end-expiration (atelectrauma), generating high shear stress that disrupts the epithelial-endothelial barrier and triggers systemic cytokine release (biotrauma)
options.explanation: Ventilator-Induced Lung Injury (VILI) is a severe iatrogenic complication of mechanical ventilation that encompasses three interrelated mechanical and biological mechanisms: (1) VOLUTRAUMA: Historically attributed to high airway pressure (barotrauma), seminal trials (e.g., ARDSNet 2000) demonstrated that EXCESSIVE END-INSPIRATORY ALVEOLAR OVERDISTENSION (volutrauma from high tidal volumes, e.g., 12 mL/kg) is the primary driver of lung damage. In ARDS, the aerated lung volume is severely reduced ('baby lung'); delivering normal tidal volumes severely overstretches these few patent alveoli. (2) ATELECTRAUMA: Ventilating with inadequate or zero positive end-expiratory pressure (ZEEP) allows unstable, surfactant-deficient alveoli to COLLAPSE AT END-EXPIRATION AND REOPEN AT INSPIRATION. This repetitive cyclic opening and closing generates catastrophic interfacial SHEAR FORCES that rip alveolar epithelial and capillary endothelial cells apart. (3) BIOTRAUMA: Mechanical deformation activates mechanosensitive ion channels and cell signaling pathways, triggering massive de novo synthesis and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-8). These cytokines spill over into the systemic circulation, driving distant end-organ failure (acute kidney injury, vasoplegic shock, multiorgan dysfunction syndrome). Lung-protective ventilation (6 mL/kg PBW, plateau pressure < 30 cm H2O, adequate PEEP) directly mitigates volutrauma, atelectrauma, and biotrauma.
